name: Osman Antireflux Trial
question: Does a serous-lined extramural ureteral tunnel prevent reflux more effectively than a T-limb in orthotopic ileal substitution?

design.population: Sixty patients (41 men, 19 women) with invasive bladder cancer undergoing radical cystectomy and orthotopic ileal bladder substitution.
design.description: Prospective comparison randomized by opaque sealed envelope: 30 patients (55 renal units) per arm; group 1 received an ileal W neobladder with a serous-lined extramural tunnel and group 2 a T-limb procedure.
design.locator: Full text, Patients and Methods, p 1518; Table 1, p 1519

verdictNote: Less reflux with the tunnel; cortical scarring occurred in three versus four renal units.
takeaway: In randomized groups receiving a serous-lined extramural tunnel or T-limb, at mean follow-up of 6.3 versus 7.4 months, ascending studies found reflux in 0/49 versus 13/45 evaluable renal units (29%; P < 0.01); ureteroileal stricture occurred in one unit per arm.

reports.label: Randomized comparison
reports.citation: Osman Y, Abol-Enein H, El-Mekresh M, et al. "Comparison between a serous-lined extramural tunnel and T-limb ileal procedure as an antireflux technique in orthotopic ileal substitutes: a prospective randomized trial." *BJU Int.* 2009;104(10):1518-1521.
reports.followUp: Mean 6.3 (SD 0.5) months in the tunnel group and 7.4 (SD 1.9) months in the T-limb group among evaluable patients
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Table 2 and Results, p 1519

results.measure: Refluxing renal units among evaluated units
results.note: The report does not designate a primary endpoint; the stated significance threshold was P < 0.05. Results are from evaluable renal units, not all randomized patients.
results.locator: Full text, Patients and Methods and Table 2, p 1519

results.measure: Renal units with progressive scarring, with or without >25% GFR reduction
results.note: The report does not designate this as a secondary endpoint or give a between-arm test.
results.locator: Full text, Table 3 and Results, pp 1519–1520

results.endpoint: GFR deterioration in refluxing T-limb units
results.measure: >25% GFR reduction among refluxing T-limb renal units
results.note: One of the 13 refluxing T-limb units had progressive cortical scarring; Table 3 shows no overlap with the three units with GFR deterioration.
results.locator: Full text, Table 3, p 1519; Results, p 1520

results.measure: >25% GFR reduction among evaluated renal units
results.note: Counts sum the GFR-deterioration and combined scarring/GFR-deterioration rows across reflux and stricture categories; no between-arm test reported.

harms.label: Ureteroileal stricture
harms.note: One evaluated renal unit in each group; Table 2 gives P = 0.51.

harms.label: Early urinary leak
harms.note: Tunnel-arm leak treated with percutaneous drain and longer urethral catheterization; T-limb leak treated with temporary percutaneous nephrostomy.

harms.label: Temporary anastomotic oedema with obstruction
harms.locator: Full text, Results, p 1519; Discussion, p 1520
harms.note: T-limb patients required temporary percutaneous nephrostomy; oedema resolved within 4 and 6 weeks.

delivery.label: Evaluable follow-up
delivery.locator: Full text, Table 1 and Results, p 1519
delivery.note: 30 patients (55 renal units) randomized per arm; 50/60 contributed follow-up imaging. Ten were unevaluable: three perioperative deaths, five oncological failures and two drug-induced renal failures; reasons by arm not reported.

delivery.label: Upper-tract assessment
delivery.value: Baseline intravenous urography, isotope GFR assessment and 99mTc-DMSA cortical imaging; repeat imaging and ascending studies in evaluable patients.
delivery.locator: Full text, Patients and Methods, pp 1518–1519

delivery.label: Ascending-study protocol
delivery.value: Water-soluble contrast and saline infused from a container 50 cm above the patient until reflux or maximum pouch capacity; postero-anterior and oblique views obtained.
delivery.locator: Full text, Patients and Methods, p 1519
